algorithm.reason: Full unbounded LFT spigot with growing signed integer state; evaluate floor((3*q+r)/t) and floor((4*q+r)/t) for every tested candidate, emit exactly n digits with the prescribed grouping and counters. Ordinary pure-Elm arbitrary-precision library; large-by-small multiplication operand order is a general arithmetic optimization, not an input-specific shortcut.

Sequential unbounded spigot written in Mech with general GMP-backed bigint operations. Both extract(3) and extract(4) are evaluated for each tested candidate. The advance variant uses the same impossible-candidate guard as the pinned Rust #4 source; no alternative pi algorithm or digit cache.

Four source functions: coefficient, apply, apply-transpose, and step. Twenty power-method applications execute forty matrix-vector products. Coefficients are computed by emitted Mech arithmetic; no stored matrix or answer shortcut.
Full symplectic pair integration is written in Mech. The generic reactive runner supplies iteration count and output formatting; it contains no gravity kernel.

The Mech-defined callback performs double-precision escape iteration for every pixel, with a maximum of 50 iterations, and emits the complete PBM. Native SIMD and lane termination preserve that algorithm.

Nine independent regex counts, each using its prescribed pattern, and five ordered regex substitutions. The general regex library handles each operation; there is no combined-pattern benchmark matcher.

Full bottom-up construction and traversal of distinct ordinary nodes, including equally allocated leaves. Uses the general core library memory pool through memory/with-arena and memory/with-frame. This allocation strategy must be disclosed; it is not a default-GC comparison.
algorithm.allocation_policy: General core library pool; distinct 16-byte node slots; per-tree frame release.

algorithm.reason: The Mech program enumerates all factorial permutations in the required factoradic order, performs actual prefix flips, and reduces the alternating checksum and maximum. Parallel ranges cover the full permutation domain.

Strict comparison disables the general exact-integer-cutoff transform. Emitted objects retain floating division/comparison. Each random nucleotide advances the naive LCG. The only repeated-sequence cache is for the supplied fixed ALU string.

All overlapping keys at all seven lengths perform a library hash-table entry lookup/update. No query-only search or indexed-count substitute. The runtime checks each merged histogram total against its window count.
Buffered growing record input; full record reversal, alphabet translation, and 60-column output. The implementation does not use file size to preallocate stdin.

protocol: Fresh process startup, language/module/library loading, complete input, computation, complete output to a regular file, and shutdown are timed. Compilation, validation and hashing are excluded. All timings are local; three sequential shuffled full-workload samples, unchanged Mech controls, AC power and Low Power Mode off. Concurrent compilers/power changes invalidate a sample.

release.name: dev-2026-10
release.body:
## New Language Features
* [#7664]: Allow `bit_set` to be backed by arrays of integers

## New Compiler Improvements
### Speedups
* [#7720]: LLVM Backend Performance Improvements to Reduce Compile Times Part 1
* [#7729]: LLVM Backend Performance Improvements to Reduce Compile Times Part 2
* [#7747]: Compiler Performance Improvements to Reduce Compile Times Part 3
* [#7685]: Complete Parapoly Rewrite + Race condition fixes
* [#7694]: Make global checking codegen order-independent
* [#7686]: Parse integer literals without allocating per digit and reject non digits in their exponent
* [#7739]: Make `radlink` default linker on Windows
* [#7701]: Multithread The Entire Semantic Checker
* [#7728]: `map` performance improvements

### General fixes and improvements
* [#7654]: Experimental support for cross-linking Windows executables
* [#7788]: Add the new `-windows-sdk-root` to the `odin help build` command
* [#7497]: Fix #7488: `-vet` error in `core_builtin_soa.odin` when appending multiple empty structs to `#soa[dynamic]`
* [#7500]: Fix #5851: Detect and error on chained `offset_of` expressions

release.name: alpha4-*
release.body:
‼️ We have nightly releases for the new compiler available at [roc-lang/nightlies](https://github.com/roc-lang/nightlies/releases), platform support is limited for now but most of the Roc community is using these new nightlies.

## :new: Additions

- builtin [`List.keep_if_try!`](https://www.roc-lang.org/builtins/alpha4/List/#keep_if_try!) to do `keep_if` with an effectful function #7804
- builtins `Num.[f32,f64,dec]_[to,from]_bits` #7741
- [`Str.len`](https://www.roc-lang.org/builtins/alpha4/Str/#len) to guide Roc users :) #7732

## :wastebasket: Deprecated

- `Num.[f32,f64]_[to,from]_parts` #7741

## :bug:   Fixes

- `roc check` on file that isn't app #7870
- Language server crash when downloading something that's not in the cache #8237
- Language server stack overflow #8204
- Alias `Str.Utf8Problem` not registered in delayed aliases #8182
- `not a tag union: Alias(...` #8107
- Correct exit code when expect fails with `roc somefile.roc` #7767
- `roc format --migrate` fixes #7716
- Tutorial copy button #8077
- Fix undefined behavior in canonicalization #7835
- Fix broken links in docs #8235 813709baf1 6c09f23fe4 8bd4f2060a

## :sparkles: Improvements

- Massive build speed improvement when using many `?` #7884
- Better AI docs for packages, builtins, and platforms #8131
- Better Result docs #8220
- `roc build` no longer tries to run if the check phase did not pass #7784
- Nicer error tip on undefined symbol #7913

## Other Notable Changes

- Website has moved to its [own repo](https://github.com/roc-lang/www.roc-lang.org)

Elm 0.19.3 introduces some compiler infrastructure upgrades, giving a good foundation for the more exciting stuff in the pipeline. More info is available here:

- [Another step towards Elm 1.0](https://elm-lang.org/news/another-step-towards-elm-v1)

**There are no language changes**, so once you swap to `"elm-version": "0.19.3"` in your `elm.json` file, you should be able to proceed without any further code changes.

### Install

The links below include (1) a Mac and Windows installer and (2) 64-bit binaries for various platforms.

✨ [Install](https://guide.elm-lang.org/install/elm.html) ✨

For examples of downloading the binaries directly, read the instructions [here](https://github.com/elm/compiler/tree/main/installers/linux) or [here](https://github.com/elm/compiler/tree/main/installers/mac).
